title: Generator Künneth calculation agrees with evaluation
statement: Use the finite-field datum, $A=A_{E,n}$ and the actual operations of [sk-def-sf-operations] on separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $h_i:S_i\hookrightarrow Y_i$ be locally closed immersions, let $F_i$ be lisse sheaves of finite projective $A$-modules on $S_i$, and let $L_i\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_i,A)$. Put $E_i=Rh_{i!}F_i$, $F_i^\vee=R\mathcal Hom(F_i,A)$, $T_i=F_i^\vee\otimes^LRh_i^!L_i$, $h=h_1\times h_2$, $F=F_1\boxtimes F_2$, $L=L_1\boxtimes L_2$. Use the tensor–Hom comparison [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] and finite-projective evaluation to identify $R\mathcal Hom(E_i,L_i)$ with $Rh_{i*}T_i$. Then the following composite is the evaluation-defined $\beta$ of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](iii): apply the canonical ordinary product comparison in the first factor to $Rh_{1*}T_1\boxtimes Rh_{2*}T_2$, then in the second factor to $T_1\boxtimes Rh_{2*}T_2$, use ordinary direct-image composition to obtain $Rh_*(T_1\boxtimes T_2)$, apply $Rh_*(1_{F^\vee}\otimes\alpha_{h_1,h_2})$, and identify the result with $R\mathcal Hom(Rh_!F,L)=R\mathcal Hom(E_1\boxtimes E_2,L)$ by tensor–Hom and Ku_!. The assertion is equality of maps; it does not assume or conclude invertibility of $\alpha$ or $\beta$.

proof.text: Write $P_i=Rh_{i!}$, $H_i=Rh_{i*}$, $G_i=Rh_i^!$, $W_i=G_iL_i$, $B_i=H_iT_i$, and $P,H,G$ for the product morphism $h$. Let $\theta_i:B_i\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom(E_i,L_i)$ and $\theta:HR\mathcal Hom(F,GL)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom(PF,L)$ be the canonical tensor–Hom identifications in the statement. All inputs to the subsequent projection and adjunction maps lie in $D^b_{ctf}$: a lisse finite-projective sheaf has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$, its coefficient dual is locally its finite-projective module dual, and [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i)–(v) preserves the category under the operations used to form $W_i,T_i,B_i,F$ and $E_i$. In particular this justifies using $B_i$ as projection coefficients. The exceptional adjunction needed here is the actual constructible one, supplied at finite coefficients by [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2); the latter applies to bounded constructible inputs of etale origin and does not require an ambient exceptional-adjoint admissibility hypothesis.

source.place: Beta: tensor–Hom identifications and their bounded constructible domains.

proof.text: Let $v_i:F_i\otimes^LT_i\to W_i$ be contraction of $F_i$ with $F_i^\vee$, leaving $W_i$ unchanged. This is the evaluation under the finite-projective identification prescribed in the statement. Put $W=W_1\boxtimes W_2$ and $T=T_1\boxtimes T_2$. The corresponding contraction $v:F\otimes^LT\to W$ is $v_1\boxtimes v_2$ after signed interchange. Indeed the dual identification $F^\vee=F_1^\vee\boxtimes F_2^\vee$ sends $(\phi_1,\phi_2)$ to the functional $(x_1,x_2)\mapsto\phi_1(x_1)\phi_2(x_2)$; contracting then gives the same two scalar multiplications in either order. This formula can be checked on local finite-free presentations and their finite-projective retracts. The $F_i$ and their duals are in degree zero, so moving either across a complex introduces sign $1$; all interchanges involving the other complexes use the same Koszul symmetry of the derived tensor. Here and below tensor evaluation and currying are those of [sk-def-sf-operations](i).

source.place: Beta: F dual, finite-projective evaluation, and signed tensor interchange.

proof.text:
Write $c_i:Lh_i^*B_i\to T_i$ and $\mu_i:P_iW_i\to L_i$ for the ordinary and exceptional counits, and $u_i=v_i\circ(1_{F_i}\otimes c_i)$. Claim:
$$e_i:=\operatorname{ev}\circ(1_{E_i}\otimes\theta_i)=\mu_i\circ P_i(u_i)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{h_i,F_i,B_i}:E_i\otimes^LB_i\to L_i.$$
Apply [lem-pod-hom-chain-counit-formula] with $f=h_i$, $M=F_i$, $N=L_i$, $t=1_{A_N}$: the canonical tensor–Hom map is $\operatorname{curry}(p_N)$. Let $\varphi_i=\operatorname{curry}(v_i):T_i\xrightarrow{\sim}L_N=R\mathcal Hom(F_i,W_i)$ be the prescribed finite-projective identification, so $\theta_i=\operatorname{curry}(p_N)\circ H_i\varphi_i$. By [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws], $e_i=p_N\circ(1\otimes H_i\varphi_i)$ and $\operatorname{ev}\circ(1\otimes\varphi_i)=v_i$. Naturality of $\operatorname{PF}$ [def-exchange-projection] in its second variable gives $\operatorname{PF}_{A_N}\circ(1\otimes H_i\varphi_i)=P_i(1\otimes Lh_i^*H_i\varphi_i)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{h_i,F_i,B_i}$, and naturality of the ordinary counit of [fix-prop-adjunctions](1) gives $\varepsilon_{L_N}\circ Lh_i^*H_i\varphi_i=\varphi_i\circ c_i$. Substituting into $p_N$ gives the claim. The exceptional adjunction of the Hom-chain lemma is the constructible one of the datum, supplied in step 1; no unrestricted pro-etale adjoint is invoked.

source.place: Beta: expand the two individual tensor–Hom identifications into evaluation, ordinary counit, projection and exceptional counit.

proof.text:
Put $B=B_1\boxtimes B_2$ and let $c:B\to HT$ be the iterated ordinary product comparison of the statement. Its ordinary transpose is
$$\varepsilon_{h,T}\circ Lh^*c=c_1\boxtimes c_2:Lh^*B\to T,$$
through the monoidal pullback identifications. To check the specified order, factor $h=b\circ a$ with $a=\operatorname{id}_{S_1}\times h_2$ and $b=h_1\times\operatorname{id}_{Y_2}$. The first product map has $Lb^*$-transpose $c_1\boxtimes1_{B_2}$, by substituting the exchange-mate formula and the counit-defined ordinary projection formula of [def-exchange-projection]. The second has $La^*$-transpose $1_{T_1}\boxtimes c_2$. Transposing the composite gives $(1_{T_1}\boxtimes c_2)\circ La^*(c_1\boxtimes1_{B_2})=c_1\boxtimes c_2$. The composite-counit formula in [fix-prop-adjunctions](3) gives precisely the displayed equation after ordinary direct-image composition. This checks the maps of [sk-lem-sf-kunneth-star]; their invertibility is not used in this calculation.

source.place: Beta: twice Ku_*; take the ordinary transpose using exchange and projection definitions.

proof.text:
Let $\gamma:B\to R\mathcal Hom(PF,L)$ be the composite in the question, before precomposing in the first Hom argument with $\mathrm{Ku}_!^{-1}:E_1\boxtimes E_2\to PF$. Under the finite-projective identifications its map to $HR\mathcal Hom(F,GL)$ is $H(q)\circ c$, where $q=\alpha\circ v:F\otimes^LT\to GL$ is read as its tensor–Hom transpose. Apply [lem-pod-hom-chain-counit-formula] now with $f=h$, $M=F$, $N=L$ and $t=H(\operatorname{curry}(q))\circ c$. Naturality of the ordinary counit replaces its pullback followed by evaluation by $q\circ(1_F\otimes\varepsilon_{h,T})\circ(1_F\otimes Lh^*c)$. Step 4 therefore gives the uncurried map
$$\operatorname{uncurry}(\gamma)=\mu\circ P(\alpha)\circ P(u)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{h,F,B},$$
where $\mu:PGL\to L$ is the exceptional counit and $u=(v_1\boxtimes v_2)\circ(1_F\otimes(c_1\boxtimes c_2)):F\otimes^LLh^*B\to W$. The pullback and signed interchange constraints in this formula are those already fixed in step 2. This is the Hom-chain formula applied to a specified morphism, not an assumption that a Hom comparison is invertible.

source.place: Beta: ordinary then exceptional transpose of the displayed composite.

proof.text:
Write $K_V:P(V_1\boxtimes V_2)\to P_1V_1\boxtimes P_2V_2$ for $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ at any indicated pair. Since $\alpha$ is the exceptional transpose specified by [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](ii), the adjunct–counit identity gives
$$\mu\circ P(\alpha)=(\mu_1\boxtimes\mu_2)\circ K_W.$$
This uses [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] for $P\dashv G$. Naturality of $K$, supplied by the canonical relative product theorem [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative], then gives
$$K_W\circ P(u)=(P_1u_1\boxtimes P_2u_2)\circ K_C\circ P(\delta),$$
where $C_i=F_i\otimes^LLh_i^*B_i$ and $\delta:F\otimes^LLh^*B\to C_1\boxtimes C_2$ is signed interchange. This follows by substituting $u=(u_1\boxtimes u_2)\circ\delta$.

source.place: Beta: substitute the defining Ku_!–counit transpose of alpha and use naturality.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-exterior-projection-kunneth] to $f_i=h_i$, $M_i=F_i$, and the coefficients $B_i$ of step 1. The latter are in $D^b_{ctf}$, and locally closed immersions between the stipulated schemes are separated of finite type. Substituting its identity for $K_C P(\delta)\operatorname{PF}_{h,F,B}$ in step 6 and then step 5 yields
$$\operatorname{uncurry}(\gamma)=(e_1\boxtimes e_2)\circ\xi\circ(K_F\otimes1_B),$$
using the two identities defining $e_i$ in step 3 and bifunctoriality of external tensor. Here $\xi:(E_1\boxtimes E_2)\otimes^L(B_1\boxtimes B_2)\to(E_1\otimes^LB_1)\boxtimes(E_2\otimes^LB_2)$ is the same signed interchange. Thus the contribution of the projection formulas has been accounted for by an explicit equality of the specified geometric maps.

source.place: Beta: the projection-formula square reduces the uncurried composite to the two evaluations.

proof.text: The last identification in the statement is contravariance of internal Hom along $K_F^{-1}:E_1\boxtimes E_2\xrightarrow{\sim}PF$. Its uncurried effect is to precompose step 7 by $K_F^{-1}\otimes1_B$: this is the naturality in the first variable of the tensor–Hom adjunction of [sk-def-sf-operations](i). The adjacent $K_F$ and $K_F^{-1}$ cancel. The resulting map is exactly $(e_1\boxtimes e_2)\circ\xi$. By [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](iii), this is the uncurried evaluation defining $\beta\circ(\theta_1\boxtimes\theta_2)$; both use the same signed symmetry. Currying is a bijection by [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws], so equality of these uncurried maps proves equality of the requested maps under the specified identifications. Only the $!$-Kunneth and tensor–Hom identifications have been inverted. Neither $\alpha$ nor $\beta$ has been assumed invertible, and no invertibility conclusion about them was used.

source.place: Beta: cancel Ku_! against the final Hom identification and use uniqueness of the tensor–Hom transpose.
